evidence.anchor: System Prompt for Verification by Verbal Program

abstract_sentences.text: Achieving robust perception-reasoning synergy is a central goal for advanced Vision-Language Models (VLMs).

evidence.anchor: central goal for advanced Vision-Language Models

abstract_sentences.text: Recent advancements have pursued this goal via architectural designs or agentic workflows.
However, these approaches are often limited by static textual reasoning or complicated by the significant compute and engineering burden of external agentic complexity.
Worse, this heavy investment does not yield proportional gains, often witnessing a "seesaw effect" on perception and reasoning.

evidence.anchor: seesaw effect on perception and reasoning

abstract_sentences.text: This motivates a fundamental rethinking of the true bottleneck.

In this paper, we argue that the root cause of this trade-off is an ambiguity in modality credit assignment: when a VLM fails, is it due to flawed perception ("bad seeing") or flawed logic ("bad thinking")?
To resolve this, we introduce a reinforcement learning framework that improves perception-reasoning synergy by reliably rewarding the perception fidelity.
We explicitly decompose the generation process into interleaved perception and reasoning steps.
This decoupling enables targeted supervision on perception.
Crucially, we introduce Perception Verification (PV), leveraging a "blindfolded reasoning" proxy to reward perceptual fidelity independently of reasoning outcomes.
Furthermore, to scale training across free-form VL tasks, we propose Structured Verbal Verification, which replaces high-variance LLM judging with structured algorithmic execution.

These techniques are integrated into a Modality-Aware Credit Assignment (MoCA) mechanism, which routes rewards to the specific source of error – either bad seeing or bad thinking – enabling a single VLM to achieve simultaneous performance gains across a wide task spectrum.

evidence.anchor: simultaneous performance gains across a wide task spectrum

abstract_analysis.reports_experimental_results: 仅报告定性结果与覆盖范围，没有数字、分母、不确定性或失败率；“simultaneous performance gains”是摘要最强结果表述。

experimental_design.name: Research questions
experimental_design.description: §3 explicitly frames RQ1 as simultaneous gains and comparison to state of the art, RQ2 as the necessity of PV/SVV/MoCA components, and RQ3 as PV-reward reliability under oracle fallibility.

experimental_design.name: Policy and base model
experimental_design.description: The trainable policy is Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct-7B; the paper treats the interleaved format as a task-agnostic instruction followed by GRPO.

experimental_design.name: Verifier model
experimental_design.description: Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B is used as both the text-only PV reasoner and the Structured Verbal Verification judge.

evidence.anchor: for both perception verification and outcome verification

experimental_design.name: Training data domains
experimental_design.description: Main text names instruction/reasoning data (ViRL39K and VisualWebInstruct-Verified), perception-intensive Pixel Reasoner data, and a newly crawled modality-rich collection from arXiv, newspapers and infographics.

experimental_design.name: Perception-intensive benchmarks
experimental_design.description: V*, HRBench and InfoVQA test fine-grained recognition, hyper-resolution perception and infographic/document text extraction.

evidence.anchor: fine-grained visual recognition, OCR, or grounding

experimental_design.name: Reasoning-intensive benchmarks
experimental_design.description: MathVista, MMMU and EMMA test mathematical, multi-step and domain reasoning grounded in visual inputs.

evidence.anchor: complex logical chains, mathematical calculation, or domain knowledge

experimental_design.name: Rich-modality benchmarks
experimental_design.description: DUDE, SlideVQA and MMLongBench-Doc test layouts, tables, diagrams, slide sequences and long-context documents.

experimental_design.name: Baseline families
experimental_design.description: Table 1 compares general-ability models (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.5, Llava-OV and Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct) with capability-enhanced models (VL-Rethinker, R1-VL, Pixel Reasoner, DeepEyes, Docopilot and mPLUG-Owl3).

experimental_design.name: Evaluation quantities
experimental_design.description: Main benchmark tables report per-dataset scores; PV reports accuracy, Cohen’s κ and confusion percentages; verifier comparison reports accuracy, F1 and exact five-run consistency at T=0.7.

experimental_design.name: Ablation control
experimental_design.description: Table 2 states that all variants use the same data and base model; the factors removed are RL, PV, MoCA routing and SVV/structured verification.

experimental_design.name: PV human evaluation
experimental_design.description: N=979 rollout triplets are judged by three annotators as Sufficient/Insufficient; majority vote is the reference label.

evidence.anchor: majority vote of the three annotators

experimental_design.name: VP challenge evaluation
experimental_design.description: The appendix defines a 273-pair challenge set with 144 correct and 129 incorrect examples, including exact matches, semantic rephrasings, subtle errors and mixed-fact answers.

experimental_design.name: Training hardware and budget
experimental_design.description: Training uses 16 NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs for approximately 16 hours to convergence.

experimental_design.name: RL hyperparameters
experimental_design.description: Appendix A reports lr=1e−6 with cosine decay, global batch size 256 accumulated gradient steps, 512 rollouts per policy sync, G=8, KL β=0, outcome weight 1.0, λ=0.3, αprotect=αpunish=0.2.

evidence.anchor: learning rate of 1e−6 with a cosine decay scheduler

experimental_design.name: Random seeds
experimental_design.description: The paper does not report random seed count for the MoCA training run or benchmark evaluation; Appendix A lists hyperparameters but no seed.

experimental_design.name: Data leakage and split control
experimental_design.description: No explicit holdout/leakage protocol is given for the main benchmark suite; the VP challenge set is selected from both training and test sets, so it is a verifier check rather than an independent held-out evaluation.

claim_closure.claim: A single VLM can gain simultaneously across perception-centric, rich-modality and reasoning-centric benchmarks.
claim_closure.method_response: Interleaving exposes perception blocks and MoCA routes PV/OV credit.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 improves over the 7B base in all nine cells, but reports descriptive scores only.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The paper’s closing framing is supplied by the abstract/RQ1 result prose; no dedicated conclusion section returns the claim.

claim_closure.claim: Explicit perception/reasoning decomposition makes the error source inspectable.
claim_closure.method_response: AP recognition blocks and AR think blocks are defined and elicited by Figures 2–3.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 2–3 visibly instantiate the tag-separated trajectory.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Contribution list calls the result an interpretable, modular reasoner.

evidence.anchor: two distinct, component-level sets of actions

claim_closure.claim: PV measures perceptual sufficiency independently of final reasoning.
claim_closure.method_response: A text-only Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B receives Q and {ap} without V; success gives binary RP.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Human-majority confusion matrix reports 86.31% agreement and κ=.707.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Paper calls PV a reliable proxy, while acknowledging false-negative noise.

claim_closure.claim: SVV supplies a robust low-variance reward for free-form outcomes.
claim_closure.method_response: A universal staged verbal protocol decomposes answer typing, extraction, reconstruction and comparison.
claim_closure.evidence_response: VP reaches 92.3% five-run consistency versus 78.6% for ordinary prompting on N=273.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: No direct RL learning-curve or reward-variance measurement is shown; conclusion is confined to challenge-set behavior.

claim_closure.claim: MoCA resolves the bad-seeing/bad-thinking credit ambiguity.
claim_closure.method_response: RP gates failed-trajectory advantages, protecting correct perception tokens and punishing failed perception tokens.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Component ablations show lower benchmark scores when PV or routed credit is removed.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The paper interprets the ablation drops as evidence that MoCA logic is essential, but no token-level causal trace is measured.

claim_closure.claim: PV is robust to a fallible oracle.
claim_closure.method_response: The protect term is intended to reduce damage from false-negative PV decisions.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Human comparison identifies 9.19% false negatives versus 4.49% false positives.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The paper asserts protection, but does not run a controlled oracle-noise training experiment.

claim_closure.claim: The approach is a lightweight alternative to external agentic workflows.
claim_closure.method_response: The model internalizes perception as a block in one autoregressive generation and reuses one verifier.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 1–4 show internal flow; no latency or engineering-cost comparison is reported.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The paper calls the path lightweight and scalable without a direct cost benchmark.

evidence.anchor: same verifier for PV and OV

claim_closure.claim: The method applies to any visually grounded reasoning pattern.
claim_closure.method_response: The argument assumes task-relevant visual features can be converted to discrete textual premises.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Only image/document benchmark families and three qualitative examples are evaluated; no maze-like non-verbal grounding test appears.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: The scope is implicitly limited to explicit multimodal reasoning, despite “wide task spectrum” language.

evidence.anchor: certain visual patterns cannot be trivially converted to text

claim_closure.claim: The verifier metrics are internally consistent with the supplied labels.
claim_closure.method_response: VP prompt fixes a four-type procedure and numeric/semantic scoring rules.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 4 reports accuracy, F1 and consistency; the challenge set is partly drawn from training and test data.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Results support verifier discrimination on the constructed set, not independent deployment reliability.

evidence.anchor: selected from the both the training set and test set

final_judgment.single_storyline: 论文把 multimodal reasoning 的 seesaw trade-off 归因于 modality credit assignment ambiguity：先用 <recognition>/<think> 外显 perception 与 reasoning，再用 blindfolded PV 测视觉证据充分性、SVV 测自由回答结果，最后由 MoCA 在失败轨迹上保护正确 perception 或惩罚错误 perception。
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留问题形式化、四个核心方法图、六个核心公式、三项 RQ、主 benchmark 表、组件消融、PV–human confusion matrix、verifier challenge 表和关键代理噪声讨论；这些对象足以理解方法和主结果。
final_judgment.appendix_moves: 附录补充硬件/超参数、benchmark 定义、44,851 条训练数据构成、完整 VP prompt、VP/PV 标注设计、extended model matrix 与三个 qualitative examples。迁移没有损害核心方法自足性，但 verifier 复现实验和训练细节依赖附录。
final_judgment.best_pattern: 最有效的组合是“Figure 1 overview → Figure 2 trajectory → Figure 3/4 executable prompts → Table 1/2 decision matrices → Table 3/4 reward reliability”：视觉流程、可执行协议和逐组件对照在同一因果链中。
final_judgment.largest_gap: PV 的因果归因依赖 text-only Qwen2.5-Instruct-14B 作为近似 reasoning oracle；proxy 失败可能被当作 bad seeing。论文报告了 human agreement，却没有 oracle calibration、受控 false-negative 噪声训练或 token-level attribution 证据；主结果也没有 seed/不确定性。
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 当任务失败可来自不同模态时，应把中间证据外显，并在屏蔽原始模态的代理任务上验证证据充分性，再把独立奖励路由回对应动作块。
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适用于关键视觉事实可用文本表达、且 text-only verifier 足以判断充分性的显式 System-2 任务；对不可语言化的空间/纹理模式、弱 verifier 或需要真实连续视觉状态的任务，PV 不应被当作充分的因果监督。
